description: One aberration of 0.015 on two white shapes over a near-black bed, and the whole fixture is the difference between what it does to each. The border's band runs close to the edges of frame, where the split is at its widest: it comes back with a yellow fringe on its outer side, a cyan one on its inner side and its own white left in between, and the fringes down the left and right sides are wider than the ones along the top and bottom because those sides sit further from the centre. The pip in the middle carries the same number and comes back white, because the displacement is proportional to how far a pixel is from the layer's own centre and the pip is at it. What a wrong render looks like: fringes of one width everywhere, the pip included, means the split is uniform rather than radial and reads as a misregistration; the fringes swapped -- cyan outside, yellow inside -- means red and blue are sampled the wrong way round; no fringe at all on a frame whose shapes are otherwise right means the aberration was skipped, which is what the copy path does to a layer nothing else has touched. Unlike grain, this is a fixture the pixel gate can actually hold: the split is structure rather than texture, so it survives an encode -- see docs/golden-renders.md for the measurement, and for how narrow a split has to get before it stops surviving one.
